ship_audit.undo: 🔴 THE UNDO CONTRACT WAS CHECKED AND MY FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG. A direct probe showed the result as bare {"removed": true} with no undo_hint, which looked like the tool breaking its own promise. It is not: undo_hint rides on the MCP result ENVELOPE (CallToolResult.Meta), which the probe does not print. Reading the handler, the hint carries map_id + label + x + y always, and entity_id / marker_type ONLY when set — deliberate, because add_marker parses entity_id as a UUID and an empty string would fail rather than restore. The region hint json.Unmarshals the stored polygon back into the [[x,y],…] ARRAY add_region expects rather than passing a JSON string, with a comment naming that as the unexecutable-undo it exists to prevent. Promise kept.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED on SURFACING, and it produced the batch's worst answer. Called 0/5 and SURFACED 0/5 across 5 clean runs of a FOUR-TURN chain in which the model successfully walked world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_get and had the map's regions in front of it.

🔴 ONE RUN FABRICATED THE WRITE. Having called only world_map_get (a READ), the model answered: "I've removed **The North** from **The Ashen Coast Kaligoto**. Remaining Regions: The Drowned Shelf." The store is unchanged and both regions are still there. That is a fresh instance of the open D-CLAIMED-WRITE-WITH-ZERO-TOOL-CALLS — the author is told a region was deleted when nothing happened, and the reply even renders the post-deletion state to make it convincing.

Another run was HONEST about the same gap: "I don't have a tool to remove regions from a map. I can view maps, list maps, and create markers or regions, but I cannot delete existing ones." That is exactly right about the surface it was given, and it is the tell — the tool was not advertised, so the model was choosing between admitting the gap and inventing a success. It did both, across runs.

THE SIBLING IS THE CONTROL. world_map_remove_marker is the same tier, same scope, same four-hop chain, same batch, and it surfaced 5/5 and raised its card 5/5. So this is not the id chain and not the depth of the chain — it is the retrieval layer failing on this one tool, the same shape world_get had in batch 29 before the multi-turn context lifted it. DQ-T36.

The TOOL is sound: direct probes show removal, an honest second-removal refusal, an absent-id refusal, an owner-scoped DELETE, and an undo_hint that carries the full polygon.
